title: Moving to Opelousas and the music scene there
summary: He took a job at the St. Andrew Club in 1943, married, and brought his wife back home; rock and roll has displaced older music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Oh, when did you move up? What's the name of the town? Opelousas?

Opelousas. Well, we opened a job there at the St. Andrew Club. I was in 43. I got married a couple years after. So I'm not glad to move there. Yeah. The wife didn't want to leave there. I did take her out on a couple of trips. And I know she wasn't satisfied and she started losing weight. So I say the best for me to take her back home and just branch off from there.
Is there much music up there?
Oh, there are a lot of bands, but a lot of rock and roll people. They go for that. The kids do, but the other people, they don't go out anymore like they used to.
